corpus_param_status: fixture-corpus test parameters, NOT protocol values
note: guardian/audit/chain.py takes max_justification_chars as a required constructor argument with no default, because no protocol file owns a justification length bound yet: evaluation-protocol.md section 4 owns the Monitor's evidence caps and security-policy.md section 1.5 states the property without a number. This file is the fixture corpus supplying its own, exactly as each monitor/fixtures/<id>/fixture.yaml supplies its own corpus_cap_* values beside a corpus_cap_status sentinel, and guardian/audit/fixtures/build.py refuses to read the value unless corpus_param_status is present. The value here is the same one guardian/app/models.py bounds its Justification annotation at, so the corpus exercises the shape the running Guardian produces rather than an invented one; that agreement is a convenience and neither number is a protocol value. The missing protocol row stays missing, which is the point.
note_2: A second parameter is deliberately absent. The chain assigns seq, prev_hash and hash, and every other field of every record is a literal in build.py, so the corpus has no seed, no clock and no other tunable. Replaying build.py --check twice produces identical bytes, which is what .agents/rules/20-parity-and-determinism.md asks of anything that generates evidence.
